thread:
alex_pm: Drafting a prioritization matrix for API error handling before Q2 roadmap finalization. Wanted to capture tradeoffs across: rate limits, validation errors, model-unavailable, function-call failures, and structured-output mismatches. Goal: 1) launch MVP surface with clear client guidance, 2) define must-have server behaviors (fallbacks/retries), 3) set launch gating criteria.

rachel_eng: +1. Can we start with concrete customer stories? e.g., high-throughput chat vs. small-batch embeddings for analytics customers. Different SLOs.

sam_platform: Suggest we separate surface into three tiers: Hosted public API, Dedicated (reserved), Private. Behavior and priority differ — e.g., Dedicated gets more aggressive fallbacks.

mira_ml: For model-unavailable we need explicit mapping: return 503 with retry-after when transient, 409/422 when model variant incompatible, and an alternate-model header when we can serve a lower-fidelity variant.

jon_support: Common support volume comes from two things: ambiguous validation errors (clients unsure what to fix) and rate limits with no retry hints. Customers want a single field they can program against.

liam_security: Note: any headers exposing model variants must be opt-in for Private deployments. Legal asked we avoid leaking internal hostnames in headers.

alex_pm: Agreed. Proposal sketch below — please react with :+1: if you accept or comment with edits. We'll bake into launch WG doc.

--- priority matrix (sketch) ---
- Severity A (blocker for public launch): model-unavailable without graceful fallback; missing retry hints for 429/503; validation errors that give no field-level context.
- Severity B (must have for Dedicated / Private): inconsistent structured-output errors (JSON schema mismatch), unclear function-call errors when tool returns 500.
- Severity C (nice-to-have): richer rate-limit quotas per-token vs per-minute, quota-exhaustion dashboards.

rachel_eng: For Severity A, suggested server behavior:
```
if model_unavailable_transient:
  return 503, {"retry_after": 10, "code": "model_unavailable.transient"}
elif model_unavailable_permanent:
  return 503, {"code": "model_unavailable.permanent", "fallback_available": false}
elif fallback_available:
  return 200 with downgraded_model response and header: X-RW-Fallback-Model: <id>
```
This keeps clients in control.

sam_platform: We should standardize the error payload shape so SDKs can parse it easily. Minimal fields: code, message, retry_after (optional), details (optional). Example: 
```json
{"code":"rate_limit.exceeded","message":"token quota exceeded","retry_after":30}
```

mira_ml: For structured-output/generation where schema validation fails, add a validation path: return 422 with path to error and an example of expected shape, plus a human-friendly message. That reduces support tickets.

jon_support: +1. Example we see: clients get 'invalid_output' and have no hint which field. Please include 'schema_path' and 'example'.

liam_security: also require that any example payloads are sanitized (no customer PII). We should document allowed fields for debugging.

alex_pm: On routing/fallback policy: prioritize latency-sensitive requests -> try cheaper model only if request explicitly allows 'allow_fallback=true'. Otherwise surface a 503 with retry hint. For Dedicated customers we can make fallback-on-by-default as part of contract. Thoughts?

rachel_eng: That makes sense. Add a header: X-RW-Fallback-Used: true|false when fallback occurs. For public API default: false. For Dedicated, default per-customer config.

sam_platform: We need to cover rate limits with burst and long-term quotas. Server should return 429 with a 'quota_type' field: "per_minute", "per_token", "concurrent_streams". Helps SDKs choose backoff.

mira_ml: For function/tool calling: differentiate between tool-side errors (tool-exec 5xx) and serialization/validation errors of the call. Example codes: 'tool.exec_error', 'tool.validation_error'. Include tool_id in details.

alex_pm: Ok, launch gating checklist (draft):
- Must: documented error schema + examples (public docs).
- Must: structured-output 422 with schema_path for our standard JSON schema enforcement for function calls.
- Must: 429 + retry hints for at least per_minute quota.
- Must: model-unavailable behavior defined (503 transient with retry_after or explicit fallback header).
- Nice-to-have: header-based fallback guidance and dashboard integration.

jon_support: Timeline ask: Customers expect docs and SDK updates before GA. Can engineering deliver server + SDK changes within 3 sprints?

rachel_eng: Rough estimate: server-side: 2 sprints to standardize payloads + fallback headers; SDKs: 1 sprint per language (we'll prioritize JS/Python). Docs: 1 sprint parallel. So 3-4 sprints total to be safe.

liam_security: Add security review to the gating list for headers and examples. That will take ~1 sprint but can overlap.

sam_platform: Operational checklist: metrics to emit at launch: error_code counts, fallback_rate, retry_after distribution, per-customer rate-limit hits. Also a dashboard for on-call.

alex_pm: Great. Action items:
- rachel_eng: produce a canonical error-schema spec + example payloads (due EOD Fri).
- sam_platform: define headers and config knobs for Hosted/Dedicated/Private (due Mon).
- mira_ml: propose model-fallback policy matrix (which models allowed as fallback for each primary) (due Mon).
- jon_support: draft client-friendly troubleshooting doc snippets we can include in API docs (due Tue).
- liam_security: quick checklist for privacy-sanitization of debug examples (due Tue).

rachel_eng: I'll push a PR to /docs/error-schema with examples and a sample SDK deserializer.

alex_pm: Thanks — if no objections I'll consolidate into the roadmap doc and share with launch WG by Monday. React :thumbsup: if you're good.
